105: static int sdio_wait_command(struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv, uint32_t cmd)
106: {
107:   clock_t deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(1000);
108:   uint32_t status;
109: 
110:   for (;;)
111:     {
112:       status = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS);
113:       if ((status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
114:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
115:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT)) != 0)
116:         {
117:           break;
118:         }
119: 
120:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
121:         {
122:           printf("SDIO CMD%u timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
123:                  (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
124:                  (unsigned long)status);
125:           return -ETIMEDOUT;
126:         }
127: 
128:       /* At transfer speed the RX FIFO can fill before a 100 us sleep
129:        * expires.  Keep the PIO loop tight while data is active; otherwise a
130:        * 512-byte sector consistently overflows after the first 256 bytes. */
131:       if (!priv->data_active)
132:         {
133:           nxsig_usleep(100);
134:         }
135:     }
136: 
137:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
138:              status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
139:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
140:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT |
141:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_OK |
142:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL));
143: 
144:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT) != 0)
145:     {
146:       printf("SDIO CMD%u response timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
147:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
148:              (unsigned long)status);
149:       return -ETIMEDOUT;
150:     }
151: 
152:   /* The BK7258 host reports CRC failure for the open-drain/long-response
153:    * identification commands even when the vendor stack accepts the response.
154:    * Armino explicitly tolerates this for ACMD41, CMD2 and CMD9.  Keep the
155:    * same compatibility rule while preserving CRC errors for normal R1/R7.
156:    */
157:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL) != 0 &&
158:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != SD_ACMDIDX41 &&
159:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX2 &&
160:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX9)
161:     {
162:       printf("SDIO CMD%u CRC error status=0x%08lx\n",
163:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
164:              (unsigned long)status);
165:       return -EIO;
166:     }
167: 
168:   return OK;
169: }

171: static int sdio_sendcmd(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev, uint32_t cmd,
172:                         uint32_t arg)
173: {
174:   uint32_t response;
175:   uint32_t value;
176: 
177:   response = (cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK) >> MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT;
178:   value = ((cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) << BK7258_SDIO_CMD_INDEX_SHIFT);
179:   if (response != MMCSD_NO_RESPONSE)
180:     {
181:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE;
182:     }
183:   if (response == MMCSD_R2_RESPONSE)
184:     {
185:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_CMD_LONG;
186:     }
187:   if (response != MMCSD_NO_RESPONSE &&
188:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX2 &&
189:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX9 &&
190:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != SD_ACMDIDX41)
191:     {
192:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_CHECK;
193:     }
194: 
195:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_CMD_ARGUMENT, arg);
196:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CTRL, value | BK7258_SDIO_CMD_START);
197:   return OK;
198: }

407: static void sdio_drain_fifo(FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv)
408: {
409:   unsigned int count = 4;
410: 
411:   while (priv->remaining != 0 && count-- != 0 &&
412:          (sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO) & BK7258_SDIO_RX_READY) != 0)
413:     {
414:       uint32_t word = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_RX_FIFO);
415:       size_t copy = priv->remaining < sizeof(word) ? priv->remaining :
416:                     sizeof(word);
417: 
418:       memcpy(priv->buffer, &word, copy);
419:       priv->buffer += copy;
420:       priv->remaining -= copy;
421: 
422:       /* At the 100 kHz validation clock a 32-bit word takes 320 us on the
423:        * 1-bit bus.  Pace reads so a stale RX_READY sample cannot consume the
424:        * same FIFO slot repeatedly before the peripheral updates its state. */
425:       up_udelay(300);
426:     }
427: }

562: static sdio_eventset_t sdio_eventwait(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev)
563: {
564:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
565:   clock_t deadline = priv->wait_start + MSEC2TICK(priv->wait_timeout);
566: 
567:   for (;;)
568:     {
569:       uint32_t status = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS);
570: 
571:       if (priv->data_active)
572:         {
573:           sdio_drain_fifo(priv);
574:         }
575: 
576:       if (priv->data_active && priv->blocklen == 512 &&
577:           priv->remaining == 0)
578:         {
579:           priv->data_active = false;
580:           priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE;
581:           break;
582:         }
583: 
584:       if ((status & (BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
585:                       BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_FAIL |
586:                       BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_OVERFLOW)) != 0)
587:         {
588:           clock_t drain_deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(10);
589: 
590:           while (priv->remaining != 0 &&
591:                  (int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - drain_deadline) < 0)
592:             {
593:               sdio_drain_fifo(priv);
594:             }
595: 
596:           printf("SDIO data error status=0x%08lx remaining=%lu\n",
597:                  (unsigned long)status, (unsigned long)priv->remaining);
598:           sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
599:                       status & (BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
600:                                 BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
601:                                 BK7258_SDIO_RX_NEED_READ |
602:                                 BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_FAIL |
603:                                 BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_OVERFLOW |
604:                                 BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_OK));
605:           priv->data_active = false;
606:           if ((status & (BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
607:                          BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_OVERFLOW)) == 0 &&
608:               priv->remaining == 0)
609:             {
610:               /* BK7258 V2 can raise DATA_CRC_FAIL for its post-block
611:                * pre-read state.  The payload is usable only when the whole
612:                * requested block was drained and no timeout/overflow occurred. */
613:               priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE;
614:             }
615:           else
616:             {
617:               priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_ERROR;
618:             }
619:           break;
620:         }
621: 
622:       if (priv->data_active &&
623:           (status & BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END) != 0)
624:         {
625:           sdio_drain_fifo(priv);
626:           sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
627:                      status & (BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
628:                                BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_OK |
629:                                BK7258_SDIO_RX_NEED_READ));
630:           priv->data_active = false;
631:           priv->wake_events = priv->remaining == 0 ?
632:                               SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE : SDIOWAIT_ERROR;
633:           printf("SDIO data complete status=0x%08lx remaining=%lu event=0x%x\n",
634:                  (unsigned long)status, (unsigned long)priv->remaining,
635:                  priv->wake_events);
636:           break;
637:         }
638: 
639:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
640:         {
641:           priv->data_active = false;
642:           priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT;
643:           printf("SDIO data timeout status=0x%08lx remaining=%lu\n",
644:                  (unsigned long)status, (unsigned long)priv->remaining);
645:           break;
646:         }
647: 
648:       if (!priv->data_active)
649:         {
650:           nxsig_usleep(100);
651:         }
652:     }
653: 
654:   priv->wait_events = 0;
655:   return priv->wake_events;

241: /* CMD8 */
242: static bk_err_t sd_card_cmd_send_if_cond(void)
243: {
244: 	bk_err_t error_state = 0;
245: 	uint32_t rsp_arg = 0;
246: 	uint8_t voltage_accpet, check_pattern = 0;
247: 	sdio_host_cmd_cfg_t cmd_cfg = {0};
248: 	uint32_t retry_cnt = SD_CARD_MAX_CMD_TRIAL_COUNT;
249: 
250: 	/* Send CMD8 to verify SD card interface operation condition
251: 	 * Argument:
252: 	 *  - [31:12]: Reserved (shall be set to '0')
253: 	 *  - [11:8]: Support Voltage (VHS) 0x1 (Range: 2.7-3.6 V)
254: 	 *  - [7:0]: Check Pattern (recommand 0xAA)
255: 	 * CMD Response: R7
256: 	 */
257: 	cmd_cfg.cmd_index = SD_CMD_SEND_IF_COND;
258: 	cmd_cfg.argument = SD_CHECK_PATTERN;
259: 	cmd_cfg.response = SDIO_HOST_CMD_RSP_SHORT;
260: 	cmd_cfg.wait_rsp_timeout = sd_card_get_cmd_timeout_param();
261: 	cmd_cfg.crc_check = true;
262: 
263: 	while(retry_cnt)
264: 	{
265: 		retry_cnt--;
266: 
267: 		bk_sdio_host_send_command(&cmd_cfg);
268: 		error_state = bk_sdio_host_wait_cmd_response(cmd_cfg.cmd_index);
269: 		if (error_state == BK_OK)
270: 			break;
271: 	}
272: 	if((error_state != BK_OK))
273: 	{
274: 		SD_CARD_LOGW("CMD8 SEND_IF_COND err:-%x\r\n", -error_state);
275: 		return error_state;
276: 	}
277: 
278: 	SD_CARD_LOGV("sdio host send CMD8(SEND_IF_COND) ok\r\n");
279: 
280: 	/* Get Response R7 argument
281: 	 * - [11:8]: Voltage accepted
282: 	 * - [7:0]: Echo-back of check pattern
283: 	 * Voltage accepted:
284: 	 *  -0000b: Not Defined
285: 	 *  -0001b: 2.7-3.6 V
286: 	 */
287: 	rsp_arg = bk_sdio_host_get_cmd_rsp_argument(SDIO_HOST_RSP0);
288: 	check_pattern = rsp_arg & 0xff;
289: 	voltage_accpet = (rsp_arg >> 8) & 0xf;
290: 
291: 	if (check_pattern == 0xaa && voltage_accpet == 0x1) {
292: 		SD_CARD_LOGD("sd card support voltage 2.7-3.6 V\r\n");
293: 		return BK_OK;
294: 	} else {
295: 		SD_CARD_LOGW("sd card unsupport voltage\r\n");
296: 		return BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_INVALID_VOLT_RANGE;
297: 	}
298: 
299: 	return error_state;
300: }

835: static bk_err_t sd_card_power_on(void)
836: {
837: 	bk_err_t error_state;
838: 	uint32_t count = 0, valid_volt = 0;
839: 	uint32_t response = 0;
840: 
841: 	/* CMD0: GO_IDLE_STATE */
842: 	error_state = sd_card_cmd_go_idle_state();
843: 	if (error_state != BK_OK) {
844: 		return error_state;
845: 	}
846:     rtos_delay_milliseconds(50);
847: 
848: 	/* CMD8: SEND_IF_COND: Command available on V2.0 cards */
849: 	error_state = sd_card_cmd_send_if_cond();
850: 	if (error_state != BK_OK) {
851: 		s_sd_card_obj.sd_card.card_version = SD_CARD_V1_X;
852: 	} else {
853: 		s_sd_card_obj.sd_card.card_version = SD_CARD_V2_X;
854: 	}
855: 
856: 	if (s_sd_card_obj.sd_card.card_version == SD_CARD_V2_X) {
857: 		/* SEND CMD55 APP_CMD with RCA as 0 */
858: 		error_state = sd_card_cmd_app_cmd(0);
859: 		if (error_state != BK_OK) {
860: 			SD_CARD_LOGW("unsupported feature\r\n");
861: 			return BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE;
862: 		}
863: 	}
864: 
865: 	while ((count < SD_CARD_MAX_VOLT_TRIAL_COUNT) && (valid_volt == 0)) {
866: 		/* Send CMD55 APP_CMD with RCA as 0 */
867: 		error_state = sd_card_cmd_app_cmd(0);
868: 		if (error_state != BK_OK) {
869: 			return error_state;
870: 		}
871: 
872: 		/* Send ACMD41 */
873: 		error_state = sd_card_cmd_sd_send_op_cond(SD_DEFAULT_OCR);
874: 		if (error_state != BK_OK) {
875: 			SD_CARD_LOGW("unsupported feature\r\n");
876: 			return BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE;
877: 		}
878: 		/* Get command response */
879: 		response = bk_sdio_host_get_cmd_rsp_argument(SDIO_HOST_RSP0);
880: 
881: 		/* Get operating voltage
882: 		 * OCR register:
883: 		 * BIT[31]: card power up status bit
884: 		 */
885: 		valid_volt = (((response >> 31) == 1) ? 1 : 0);
886: 
887: 		count++;
888: 		rtos_delay_milliseconds(2);
889: 	}
890: 
891: 	if (count >= SD_CARD_MAX_VOLT_TRIAL_COUNT) {
892: 		SD_CARD_LOGW("send cmd55 and acmd41 retry time out\r\n");
893: 		return BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_INVALID_VOLT_RANGE;
894: 	}
895: 
896: 	/* OCR register BIT[30] */
897: 	if ((response & SD_OCR_HIGH_CAPACITY) == SD_OCR_HIGH_CAPACITY) {
898: 		SD_CARD_LOGD("card capacity SDHC_SDXC\r\n");
899: 		s_sd_card_obj.sd_card.card_type = SD_CARD_TYPE_SDHC_SDXC;
900: 	} else {
901: 		s_sd_card_obj.sd_card.card_type = SD_CARD_TYPE_SDSC;
902: 		SD_CARD_LOGD("card capacity SDSC\r\n");
903: 	}
904: 
905: 	return BK_OK;
906: }

1174: bk_err_t bk_sd_card_erase(uint32_t start_block_addr, uint32_t end_block_addr)
1175: {
1176: 	bk_err_t error_state = BK_OK;
1177: 	uint32_t start_addr = start_block_addr;
1178: 	uint32_t end_addr = end_block_addr;
1179: 
1180: 	/* Check if the card command class supports erase command */
1181: 	if ((s_sd_card_obj.sd_card.class & SD_SUPPORT_ERASE_CMD) == 0) {
1182: 		SD_CARD_LOGD("the card command class not support erase command\r\n");
1183: 		//return BK_FAIL;
1184: 	}
1185: 	if (s_sd_card_obj.sd_card.card_type != SD_CARD_TYPE_SDHC_SDXC) {
1186: 		start_addr *= 512;
1187: 		end_addr *= 512;
1188: 	}
1189: 
1190: 	/* Send CMD32 to set erase start addr */
1191: 	error_state = sd_card_cmd_set_erase_start_addr(start_addr);
1192: 	if (error_state != BK_OK) {
1193: 		return error_state;
1194: 	}
1195: 	rtos_delay_milliseconds(2);
1196: 
1197: 	/* Send CMD33 to set erase end addr */
1198: 	error_state = sd_card_cmd_set_erase_end_addr(end_addr);
1199: 	if (error_state != BK_OK) {
1200: 		return error_state;
1201: 	}
1202: 	rtos_delay_milliseconds(2);
1203: 
1204: 	/* Send CMD38 ERASE */
1205: 	error_state = sd_card_cmd_erase();
1206: 	if (error_state != BK_OK) {
1207: 		return error_state;
1208: 	}
1209: 
1210: 	return BK_OK;
1211: }

462: bk_err_t bk_sdio_host_driver_init(void)
463: {
464: 	bk_err_t ret = BK_OK;
465: 	if (s_sdio_host_driver_is_init) {
466: 		SDIO_HOST_LOGV("bk_sdio_host_driver_init has inited\r\n");
467: 		return BK_OK;
468: 	}
469: 
470: 	os_memset(&s_sdio_host, 0, sizeof(s_sdio_host));
471: #if (CONFIG_SDIO_PM_CB_SUPPORT)
472: 	bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(PM_POWER_SUB_MODULE_NAME_BAKP_SDIO, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON);
473: #endif
474: 	sdio_host_hal_init(&s_sdio_host.hal);
475: #if (CONFIG_SDIO_PM_CB_SUPPORT)
476: 	int id = 0;
477: 	pm_cb_conf_t enter_config = {bk_sdio_backup, (void *)id};
478: 	pm_cb_conf_t exit_config = {bk_sdio_restore, (void *)id};
479: 	bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(PM_POWER_SUB_MODULE_NAME_BAKP_SDIO, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON);
480: 	bk_pm_sleep_register_cb(PM_MODE_LOW_VOLTAGE, PM_DEV_ID_SDIO, &enter_config, &exit_config);
481: #endif
482: 	bk_int_isr_register(INT_SRC_SDIO, sdio_host_isr, NULL);
483: 
484: 	if (s_sdio_host.irq_cmd_msg == NULL) {
485: 		ret = rtos_init_queue(
486: 								&s_sdio_host.irq_cmd_msg,
487: 								"sdio_host_queue",
488: 								4,
489: 								16
490: 							);
491: 		BK_ASSERT(kNoErr == ret); /* ASSERT VERIFIED */
492: 	}
493: 	if (s_sdio_host.tx_sema == NULL) {
494: 		int ret = rtos_init_semaphore(&(s_sdio_host.tx_sema), 1);
495: 		BK_ASSERT(kNoErr == ret); /* ASSERT VERIFIED */
496: 	}
497: 	s_sdio_host.is_tx_blocked = false;
498: 
499: 	if (s_sdio_host.rx_sema == NULL) {
500: 		int ret = rtos_init_semaphore(&(s_sdio_host.rx_sema), 1);
501: 		BK_ASSERT(kNoErr == ret); /* ASSERT VERIFIED */
502: 	}
503: 	s_sdio_host_driver_is_init = true;
504: 	return BK_OK;
505: }

507: bk_err_t bk_sdio_host_driver_deinit(void)
508: {
509: 	bk_err_t ret = BK_OK;
510: 	if (!s_sdio_host_driver_is_init) {
511: 		return BK_OK;
512: 	}
513: 	sdio_host_deinit_common();
514: #if (CONFIG_SDIO_PM_CB_SUPPORT)
515: 	bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(PM_POWER_SUB_MODULE_NAME_BAKP_SDIO, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF);
516: #endif
517: 	bk_int_isr_unregister(INT_SRC_SDIO);
518: #if (CONFIG_SDIO_PM_CB_SUPPORT)
519: 	bk_pm_sleep_unregister_cb(PM_MODE_LOW_VOLTAGE, PM_DEV_ID_SDIO, true, true);
520: 	bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(PM_POWER_SUB_MODULE_NAME_BAKP_SDIO, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF);
521: #endif
522: 
523: 	if (s_sdio_host.irq_cmd_msg) {
524: 		ret = rtos_deinit_queue(&s_sdio_host.irq_cmd_msg);
525: 		BK_ASSERT(kNoErr == ret); /* ASSERT VERIFIED */
526: 
527: 		s_sdio_host.irq_cmd_msg = NULL;
528: 	}
529: 
530: 	if (s_sdio_host.tx_sema) {
531: 		int ret = rtos_deinit_semaphore(&(s_sdio_host.tx_sema));
532: 		BK_ASSERT(kNoErr == ret); /* ASSERT VERIFIED */
533: 
534: 		s_sdio_host.tx_sema = NULL;

764: {
765: #if CONFIG_SDIO_V2P0
766: 	bk_err_t ret = BK_OK;
767: 	uint32_t msg = 0;
768: #endif
769: 
770: 	SDIO_HOST_RETURN_ON_NOT_INIT();
771: 	SDIO_PM_CHECK_RESTORE(0);
772: 
773: 	uint32_t int_status = sdio_host_hal_get_interrupt_status(&s_sdio_host.hal);
774: 
775: #if CONFIG_SDIO_V2P0
776: 	{
777: 		//TODO:Timeout and CRC fail should use different case
778: 		//FreeRTOS doesn't use EVENT,so use msg queue.
779: 		ret = rtos_pop_from_queue(&s_sdio_host.irq_cmd_msg, &msg, SDIO_CMD_WAIT_TIME);
780: 		if(ret)
781: 		{
782: 			SDIO_HOST_LOGV("sdio wait slave CMD%d timeout, int_status=0x%x, ret=%d\r\n", cmd_index, int_status, ret);
783: 			return BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_CMD_RSP_TIMEOUT;
784: 		}
785: 	}
786: #else
787: 	/* wait until cmd response */
788: 	BK_WHILE (!sdio_host_hal_is_cmd_rsp_interrupt_triggered(&s_sdio_host.hal, int_status)) {
789: 		int_status = sdio_host_hal_get_interrupt_status(&s_sdio_host.hal);
790: 	}
791: 
792: 	/* clear command response int status */
793: 	sdio_host_hal_clear_cmd_rsp_interrupt_status(&s_sdio_host.hal, int_status);
794: 
795: 	if (sdio_host_hal_is_cmd_rsp_timeout_interrupt_triggered(&s_sdio_host.hal, int_status)) {
796: 		if (cmd_index != SEND_OP_COND) {
797: 			SDIO_HOST_LOGW("sdio wait slave CMD%d timeout\r\n", cmd_index);
798: 			return BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_CMD_RSP_TIMEOUT;
799: 		}
800: 	}
801: 
802: 	if (sdio_host_hal_is_cmd_rsp_crc_fail_interrupt_triggered(&s_sdio_host.hal, int_status)) {
803: 		if ((cmd_index != SD_APP_OP_COND) &&
804: 			(cmd_index != ALL_SEND_CID) &&
805: 			(cmd_index != SEND_CSD) &&
806: 			(cmd_index != SEND_OP_COND)) {
807: 			SDIO_HOST_LOGW("sdio receive slave CMD%d crc fail\r\n", cmd_index);
808: 			return BK_ERR_SDIO_HOST_CMD_RSP_CRC_FAIL;
809: 		}
810: 	}
811: #endif
812: 	return BK_OK;
813: }

1779: /* size unit: sector counts,default sector size is 512 bytes */
1780: uint32_t bk_sd_card_get_card_size(void)
1781: {
1782: 	sd_card_csd_t *csd_p = (sd_card_csd_t *)&s_sd_card_obj.csd;
1783: 	uint32_t ver = 0, size = 0;
1784: 
1785: 	//csd_structure-0:ver1.0; 1:ver2.0; 2:ver3.0
1786: 	ver = csd_p->csd_3.csd_structure+1;
1787: 	switch(ver)
1788: 	{
1789: 		case 1:	//ver1.0
1790: 		{
1791: 			uint32_t c_size, c_size_mul, block_nr, block_len, read_bl_len;
1792: 			c_size = (csd_p->csd_2.v1p0.c_size_high<<2) + csd_p->csd_1.v1p0.c_size_low;
1793: 			c_size_mul = 1 << (csd_p->csd_1.v1p0.c_size_mult + 2);
1794: 			block_nr = (c_size + 1) * c_size_mul;
1795: 			size = block_nr;
1796: 
1797: 			read_bl_len = csd_p->csd_2.v1p0.read_bl_len;
1798: 			if(read_bl_len > 9)	//default:read_bl_len == 9;
1799: 			{
1800: 				block_len = 1 << read_bl_len;
1801: 				size = block_nr * block_len;

1803: 				size = size / (SD_BLOCK_SIZE);  // retutn sector for fatfs using, fatfs default SD_BLOCK_SIZE is 512
1804: 			}
1805: 
1806: 			break;
1807: 		}
1808: 
1809: 		case 2:	//ver2.0:(c_size:22bits == c_size_low << 16 + c_size_high), card_size == (c_size + 1) * 512 K bytes
1810: 		{
1811: 			size = ((csd_p->csd_2.v2p0.c_size_high<<16) + (csd_p->csd_1.v2p0_v3p0.c_size_low) + 1) << 10;
1812: 			break;
1813: 		}
1814: 
1815: 		case 3:	//3.0:(c_size:28bits == c_size_low << 16 + c_size_high), card_size == (c_size + 1) * 512 K bytes
1816: 		{
1817: 			size = ((csd_p->csd_2.v3p0.c_size_high<<16) + (csd_p->csd_1.v2p0_v3p0.c_size_low) + 1) << 10;
1818: 			break;
1819: 		}
1820: 
1821: 		default:
1822: 			SD_CARD_LOGE("card ver=%d.0\r\n", ver);
1823: 			break;
1824: 	}
1825: 
1826: 	SD_CARD_LOGD("card ver=%d.0,size:0x%08x sector(sector=512bytes)\r\n", ver, (uint32_t)size);
1827: 	return size;
1828: }

155: 			uint32_t tx_fifo_reset                  : 1;  //0xd[17],write fifo reset, high active; Host/Slave:Reset self state,0x1,R/W1C
156: 			uint32_t rx_fifo_rd_ready               : 1;  //0xd[18],host/slave rx fifo not empty,0x0,R
157: 			uint32_t tx_fifo_wr_ready               : 1;  //0xd[19],host/slave tx fifo not full(data is valid, not used for CMD),0x1,R
158: 			uint32_t sd_state_reset                 : 1;  //0xd[20],sdcard command and data state reset, high active; Host/Slave:Reset self state; It's better to reset after one round transfer.,0x1,R/W1C
159: 			uint32_t sd_clk_sel                     : 2;  //0xd[22:21],sdcard clock div sel, used or not depend on project; Invalid.,0x3,RW
160: 			uint32_t sd_rd_wait_sel                 : 1;  //0xd[23],read data after command ?; Use default value.,0x1,RW
161: 			uint32_t sd_wr_wait_sel                 : 1;  //0xd[24],write data after command ?; Use default value.,0x0,RW

163: 			uint32_t samp_sel                       : 1;  //0xd[26],sample egde of data 0：neg 1：pos
164: 			uint32_t clk_gate_on                    : 1;  //0xd[27],module clockgate on control 1：always on

166: 			uint32_t host_rd_blk_en                 : 1;  //0xd[29],new multi-block read  method enable

text:
## Findings

### 1. The current read-block configuration does not match the BK7258 vendor path

The strongest mismatch is the programmed read block-size field.

- Current OpenVela deliberately programs multiblock mode with a **zero block-size field** for 512-byte reads:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:350-364`
  - The comment at lines 352-354 claims that the vendor lower half leaves the read block-size field at zero.

- The BK7258 vendor HAL does not do that. `sdio_host_ll_set_read_multi_block_data()` programs:
  - multiblock mode,
  - one-bit/four-bit mode,
  - `sd_data_blk = block_size & 0xfff`,
  - receive-byte swapping.
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/sdio_ll.h:260-279`

- The zero-size exception is guarded by `CONFIG_SOC_BK7256XX`:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/sdio_ll.h:270-274`
  - The BK7258 vendor configuration selects `CONFIG_SOC_BK7258=y`, not `CONFIG_SOC_BK7256XX`:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/bk7258_ap.defconfig:7`

- The card layer passes `SD_BLOCK_SIZE`, i.e. 512, into that HAL:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:1600-1606`

- It also contains a legacy literal write intended to force the field to 512:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:1611`

Thus the faithful BK7258 value for `DATA_CTRL` during CMD18 is:

```text
DATA_ENABLE | DATA_MULTIBLOCK | DATA_BYTE_SELECT | (512 << 4)
```

plus the selected bus-width bit. Leaving `[15:4]` zero can prevent proper 512-byte framing and is a direct candidate for receiving a shifted/truncated/pre-read stream.

---

### 2. The PIO receive algorithm is substantially different from the vendor implementation

The vendor waits for a complete, CRC-valid block before draining exactly 512 bytes.

- Vendor ISR posts `rx_sema` only when receive-end/timeout is present and `DATA_CRC_OK` is asserted:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:1390-1407`

- On CRC failure, the vendor resets the SD/FIFO state, records an error, and wakes the waiter with an error:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:1408-1424`

- The PIO reader then consumes exactly 128 words for each 512-byte block:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:1199-1228`

- Each FIFO word is obtained by polling `RX_FIFO_RD_READY`, with a bounded one-microsecond polling loop, then reading exactly once:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:1178-1196`

The current implementation instead streams words concurrently with reception:

- It reads up to four words per pass:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:407-427`

- It inserts a fixed 300 µs delay after every read:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:422-425`

- It declares success as soon as 512 bytes have been copied, without waiting for receive-end or CRC status:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:576-581`

- It can also declare success after `DATA_CRC_FAIL` merely because all requested bytes happened to be drained:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:584-619`

- The receive-end branch does not require `DATA_CRC_OK`:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:622-636`

This permits an incomplete, misframed, or speculative pre-read block to be accepted as a successful sector. It also makes the fixed delay dependent on the programmed SD clock and peripheral-status update latency. The vendor implementation has neither the four-word batching nor the 300 µs delay.

---

### 3. The signature displacement is consistent with FIFO/framing loss, not byte endianness

If the `55 aa` at buffer offset 170 is the sector’s true terminal MBR signature, its expected offset is 510. The difference is:

```text
510 - 170 = 340 bytes = 85 32-bit FIFO words
```

That points to substantial data omission or to the buffer crossing into a subsequent speculative block. It is not explained by a simple byte swap.

Receive byte ordering itself matches the vendor:

- Current sets `SD_BYTE_SEL`:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_sdio.h:36`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:355-364`

- Vendor sets the same field:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/sdio_ll.h:276-278`

- Current `memcpy()` of a FIFO word on this little-endian CPU is equivalent to the vendor’s explicit low-byte-first extraction:
  - Current: `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:414-420`
  - Vendor: `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:1212-1215`

The likely causes are therefore the zero block-size field, non-vendor streaming FIFO reads, acceptance without `DATA_CRC_OK`, and stale/pre-read state after failed transfers.

---

### 4. The current implementation omits the vendor ISR/semaphore synchronization model

Vendor initialization:

- Allocates command queue, TX semaphore, and RX semaphore:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:462-503`

- Registers the SDIO ISR:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:482`

- Enables the SDIO interrupt and masks:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:325-341`

- Waits for command completion through the ISR-fed queue:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:763-812`

- Waits for received blocks through `rx_sema`:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:1047-1075`

Current OpenVela:

- Disables every SDIO interrupt mask:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:90`

- Makes `attach()` a no-op:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:304-308`

- Polls both command and data status:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:105-168`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:562-656`

The SDIO IRQ number is already available:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/irq.h:33`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/irq.h:60`

Polling command completion can remain temporarily, but the vendor block-boundary/CRC semaphore behavior should be retained for PIO reads.

---

### 5. Error handling can leave the card in CMD18 streaming state

The current helper sends CMD12 only when the entire receive path has already succeeded:

- CMD18 is accepted at:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:466-476`

- CMD12 is conditional on `ret == OK`:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:493-512`

If a timeout, overflow, or CRC failure occurs after CMD18 was accepted, the card remains in multiple-block read mode. The next read can then consume stale or speculative data before or during another CMD18, which is a plausible source of repeatable sector displacement.

The vendor CMD12 path explicitly:

1. resets SD/FIFO state,
2. forces the clock on,
3. sends CMD12 once,
4. disables TX-FIFO clock-gate influence,
5. restores automatic clock gating,
6. resets SD/FIFO state again.

References:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:649-715`
- Clock-gate semantics:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:646-715`

Current code approximately implements the bit-27 portion, but not on failed reads and not the interrupt-mask bit-13 cleanup.

---

### 6. Reset sequencing differs and the reset-bit polarity is not represented clearly

Vendor reset-to-default:

- Clears the RX reset, TX reset, and state-reset fields:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/sdio_ll.h:31-36`

- Sets RX/TX thresholds to one and enables clock recovery:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/sdio_ll.h:38-52`

Before a read, the vendor card path calls the state reset and discards any stale pre-read semaphore:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:1589-1595`

Current receive setup performs two writes using a reused register value:

- First clears thresholds, reset bits, and clock gate:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:331-335`

- Then writes thresholds and all reset bits high:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:337-340`

The vendor sources themselves contain inconsistent prose about whether these reset fields are active-high or active-low, but the operational reset helper deliberately clears the fields. The current header names:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_sdio.h:55-57`

do not describe that polarity. A single vendor-derived reset helper should replace the ad hoc two-write sequences.

---

### 7. Clock-gating during card initialization does not follow the vendor sequence

The vendor forces the SD clock continuously on for initialization:

- Before host/card initialization:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:1063-1073`

- It restores automatic clock gating only after card initialization:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:1112-1116`

Current reset/init does not set `CLOCK_GATE` bit 27:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:86-103`

It clears bit 27 when transfer clock is selected:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:289-301`

The latter is a suitable point to restore automatic gating, but identification mode should explicitly force bit 27 on first.

---

### 8. Transfer-clock programming is limited to three bits and never reaches the vendor BK7258 transfer rate

Vendor BK7258 clock encoding uses four bits `[17:14]`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/sdio_ll.h:92-96`

Clock codes include:

- `7` = 100 kHz,
- `14` = 20 MHz.
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/hal/hal_sdio_host_types.h:25-43`

Vendor defaults are:

- identification clock code 7:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/bk7258_ap.defconfig:341`
- transfer clock code 14:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/bk7258_ap.defconfig:331`

Current programming:

- clears bit 17,
- masks the code to three bits,
- defines both identification and transfer clocks as code 7.
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:74-84`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_sdio.h:63-65`

This means the current driver stays at approximately 100 kHz. That is not by itself the likely cause of the shifted signature, but it is incompatible with the vendor path and is the reason for the current non-vendor 300 µs FIFO pacing.

---

### 9. CMD18 preparation lacks the vendor stale-state and busy-card defenses

Vendor read entry:

- Checks that the preceding operation/card is no longer busy:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:1577-1587`

- The V2 busy check uses CMD55/ACMD6 until the card responds:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:1246-1280`

- Resets the host SD/FIFO state and discards the prior pre-read semaphore:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:1589-1595`

- Retries CMD18 because a card may still be busy after CMD12:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:589-620`

Current OpenVela sends CMD18 once, with no card-ready check:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:460-476`

This is especially relevant after a previous failed or delayed CMD12.

---

### 10. Card addressing is hard-coded from one observed OCR instead of tracked from card initialization

Current direct read always converts the sector to a byte address:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:466-467`

Vendor card initialization records OCR bit 30 as SDSC versus SDHC/SDXC:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:896-903`

Vendor CMD18 address conversion is conditional:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:1607-1609`

This cannot explain an offset-170 signature when reading sector zero, but it will read incorrect locations on block-addressed cards and should not remain hard-coded.

---

### 11. The fallback block driver assumes card initialization has completed

The host initializer only powers and initializes the peripheral:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:706-732`

The direct fallback reader then assumes the card is already selected, has a 512-byte block length, and is ready for CMD18:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:429-512`

The board code always unregisters the MMCSD block inode and installs the direct fallback after calling `mmcsd_slotinitialize()`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:115-145`

The vendor performs the full sequence before exposing reads:

- CMD0/CMD8/CMD55/ACMD41:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:835-905`
- CMD2/CMD3/CMD9/CMD7/ACMD6/CMD16 and transfer clock:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:908-997`

The fallback must not be used unless that equivalent card initialization has definitely completed.

---

### 12. PM/clock power-up is broadly equivalent, but the vendor also selects the source and optionally controls external card power

Current OpenVela requests the SDIO power submodule and clock and waits 30 ms:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:142-170`

Vendor host common initialization:

- powers the SDIO device clock,
- selects the 26 MHz XTAL source,
- enables the SDIO interrupt.
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:320-341`

The current divider write clears source-select bit 17, which is equivalent to selecting the low-frequency source for code 7, but the implementation should use the complete four-bit field when code 14 is selected.

Vendor external SD-card LDO control is outside the SD-card driver:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/fatfs/disk_io.c:40-72`
- It powers the card before `bk_sd_card_init()`:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/fatfs/disk_io.c:194-209`

For fixed onboard SD-NAND this may be board-specific and unnecessary, but any controllable SD-NAND rail must be enabled before the existing 30 ms initialization delay.

---

### 13. GPIO14–GPIO19 are a valid BK7258 SDIO mapping, but the one-bit vendor path only needs GPIO14–GPIO16

Vendor mapping tables show:

- GPIO14 = SDIO CLK,
- GPIO15 = SDIO CMD,
- GPIO16 = DATA0,
- GPIO17–GPIO19 = DATA1–DATA3.
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h:268-280`

Vendor one-bit GPIO setup only configures CLK, CMD, and DATA0:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:112-149`

Current configures all six pins even though it advertises one-bit-only capability:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:60-71`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:271-275`

Function zero for GPIO14–GPIO19 agrees with the vendor map, and pull-up/capacity-three settings also agree. Configuring GPIO17–GPIO19 is unnecessary in one-bit mode but is not the likely signature-shift cause.

---

### 14. The current modern register base and FIFO offsets match the canonical BK7258 CONFIG_SDIO_V2P0 path

Current definitions:

- Base `0x458d0000`,
- TX FIFO at register `0x0f`,
- RX FIFO at register `0x10`,
- threshold/state register at `0x11`.
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_sdio.h:10-23`

Vendor canonical base:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/soc/bk7258/reg_base.h:125`
- The secure vendor configuration has zero address offset:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/soc/bk7258/reg_base.h:19-29`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/bk7258_ap.defconfig:41`

Vendor FIFO addresses:

- TX `0x458d003c`,
- RX `0x458d0040`,
- threshold/state `0x458d0044`.
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/sdio_reg.h:324-379`

Therefore the current `BK7258_SDIO_RX_FIFO` definition is correct for the modern V2 aperture.

## Proposed changes

### Priority 1: Correct the 512-byte read framing

In `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:350-364`, program:

```c

        BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BYTE_SELECT |
        ((512u << BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_SHIFT) &
         BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_MASK);
```

Then set `BK7258_SDIO_DATA_ENABLE`.

Do not retain the BK7256-specific zero-block-size exception for BK7258. This is the smallest and most directly relevant correction.

### Priority 2: Replace streaming FIFO draining with the vendor block-boundary algorithm

Replace `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:407-427` and the success logic at lines 562-655 with:

1. Wait for a receive-block event that has `DATA_RECEIVE_END` and `DATA_CRC_OK`.
2. Reject `DATA_TIMEOUT`, `FIFO_OVERFLOW`, or `DATA_CRC_FAIL`.
3. After the valid block event, read exactly `blocklen / 4` FIFO words.
4. For each word, poll `RX_READY` with a bounded timeout and read once immediately.
5. Remove the fixed 300 µs delay and four-word batching.
6. Preserve low-byte-first extraction or `memcpy()` on this little-endian target.

For faithful vendor synchronization, attach `BK7258_IRQ_SDIO`, enable receive-end/data-timeout interrupts, and post a receive semaphore from the ISR. Command completion may remain polling initially if minimizing changes, but receive completion should follow the vendor ISR/semaphore model.

### Priority 3: Never accept a block without positive CRC completion

Remove both current success shortcuts:

- `remaining == 0` success at:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:576-581`
- CRC-fail-but-buffer-full success at:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:606-614`

A requested block is successful only after all 512 bytes were read and the corresponding hardware status contains `DATA_RECEIVE_END | DATA_CRC_OK`, with no timeout, overflow, or CRC-fail bit.

Treat later speculative pre-read CRC failures separately by resetting/discarding stale pre-read state before the next operation, as the vendor does.

### Priority 4: Guarantee CMD12 cleanup whenever CMD18 was accepted

Track whether CMD18 completed successfully at the command-response level. If it did, run the stop sequence even if data reception subsequently fails:

1. reset RX/TX/SD state,
2. force `CLOCK_GATE` bit 27 on,
3. send CMD12 once,
4. wait for its response,
5. clear interrupt-mask bit 13 if implemented,
6. restore automatic gating,
7. reset RX/TX/SD state again.

Apply this around `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:486-512`.

thresholds, clock recovery, sampling, and clock-gate policy.

Then explicitly set thresholds to `0x01/0x01` and clock recovery bit 25. Avoid open-coded sequences that clear all low 16 bits and then rewrite reset bits with ambiguous polarity.
